title: Exodus 25 — The oblation for the sanctuary + the ark, the mercy-seat, the table, and the lampstand

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

verdicts.reasoning: Standard speech formula; exact.

citations: Milgrom, Studies in Cultic Theology and Terminology (1983), 'The Šôq hattĕrûmâ'
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed wəyiqḥû-lî tərûmâ ... ʾăšer yiddəḇennû libbô. tərûmâ (rwm Hiphil 'lift off, set apart') is a portion set apart for the sanctuary. 'Oblation' gives that sense, is the established Ezekiel term, and keeps tərûmâ distinct from qorbān. It also has KJV precedent for tərûmâ (Isa 40:20; Ezek 45:1), and isaiah-woh 40:20 already prints it. The reception note accurately summarizes TBWTT ch. 3 (food and riches for a resident team) and adds that the Hebrew list supplies the sanctuary of vv 8-9.

zāhāḇ wāḵesep̄ ûnəḥōšeṯ: 'bronze' is the correct metal (copper/tin alloy) and NRSV usage. ASV/KJV 'brass' is obsolete English for it. Non-blocking: the note says the canon's English 'follows the ASV brass'. 'Brass' is in both the KJV and the ASV, and the canon's English generally follows the KJV, so write 'KJV/ASV'.
təḵēleṯ, ʾargāmān, tôlaʿaṯ šānî, šēš, ʿizzîm: ASV dye terms kept. 'Goats' hair' prints the ASV's bracketed supplement, which is justified by 26:7.

ʿōrōṯ ʾêlim məʾoddāmîm ... ʿōrōṯ təḥāšîm ... ʿăṣê šiṭṭîm: taḥaš is unidentified. Keeping the ASV 'sealskins' with the candidates (dugong, Egyptian ṯḥś, Akkadian dušû) in the commentary is defensible. 'Acacia' is correct.
šemen lammāʾōr ... liqṭōreṯ hassammîm: exact (ASV). The LXX lacks the verse, as the note says.
ʾaḇnê-šōham wəʾaḇnê millūʾîm: the ASV is kept, the identification of šōham is left open in the commentary, and 'stones to be set' is accurate.
wəʿāśû lî miqdāš wəšāḵantî bəṯôḵām: 'in their midst' (not 'in it') is exact.

citations: Hurowitz, I Have Built You an Exalted House (1992)
verdicts.reasoning: taḇnîṯ hammiškān wəʾēṯ taḇnîṯ kol-kēlāyw: 'pattern' is the ASV word and the lexical sense (model, plan). The reception note on TBWTT ch. 3's 'residence ... according to their plans' is accurate and kept out of the line.

ʾărôn ʿăṣê šiṭṭîm with its measurements: exact. Non-blocking: glossaryRefs is empty, although 'ark' is governed by tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25 and, once merged, by the joshua-woh central aron entry. Add the reference.
wəṣippîṯā ... mibbayiṯ ûmiḥûṣ ... zēr zāhāḇ: ASV 'crown' kept, with 'moulding' in the commentary.
paʿămōṯāyw 'its feet' (ASV, NJPS; KJV 'corners'): closer to paʿam 'foot, step'.
baddê ʿăṣê šiṭṭîm: 'poles' (NRSV) for the ASV 'staves' agrees with the signed-off 1-kings-woh 8:7-8, checked in the data.
Exact.
lōʾ yāsurû mimmennû: exact.
hāʿēḏuṯ capitalised as at exodus-woh 16:34 (checked) for the technical sense 'the tablets'.
kappōreṯ 'mercy-seat' (ASV, NRSV) is interpretive but is the established term. The commentary sets out the 'cover' and 'place of atonement' views (F9).
šənayim kərūḇîm zāhāḇ miqšâ: 'hammered work' for the ASV 'beaten work' changes nothing in the sense. 'Cherubim' follows the central entry.
min-hakkappōreṯ 'of one piece with the mercy-seat', the sense of min (Sarna 1991); exact otherwise.
pōrśê ḵənāp̄ayim ləmaʿlâ sōḵəḵîm: exact.
Exact; repeats v 16.
wənôʿaḏtî ... wəḏibbartî ʾittəḵā mēʿal hakkappōreṯ mibbên šənê hakkərūḇîm: 'meet' and 'speak with' are the lexical senses (the ASV has 'commune with'). The reception note is accurate.
Exact.
Exact (no commentary needed).
misgereṯ ṭōp̄aḥ 'a border of a handbreadth' (ASV); exact.
Exact (no commentary needed).
ləbāttîm ləḇaddîm 'as holders for the poles'; sense rendering of 'houses', literal in note.
Exact.
The four vessel names follow the ASV. The relative clause ʾăšer yussaḵ bāhēn is rendered 'with which libations are poured'. Accurate.
leḥem pānîm ləp̄ānay tāmîḏ: 'the bread of the presence' is the NRSV rendering. Unlike 'showbread', it keeps the noun the verse plays on, and NJPS 'bread of display' is recorded.

mənōraṯ zāhāḇ ṭāhôr miqšâ: 'lampstand' corrects the anachronistic 'candlestick' (the object holds oil lamps, v 37) and is the term of NRSV and NJPS. yərēḵāh wəqānāh 'its base and its shaft' is accurate.
Exact; 'lampstand' consistent.
gəḇiʿîm məšuqqāḏîm 'cups made like almond-blossoms' (ASV); 'knob' modernizes 'knop'. Exact.
Exact.
Threefold repetition preserved; exact.
kullāh miqšâ ʾaḥaṯ: exact.
wəheʿĕlâ (3ms impersonal) 'they shall set up' and wəhēʾîr ʿal-ʿēḇer pānêhā 'over against its front'. Defensible. The mounting/kindling ambiguity of heʿĕlâ is kept and noted.
ASV 'snuffers and snuff-dishes' kept; NJPS recorded.
kikkār ... yaʿăśeh ʾōṯāh (impersonal) rendered by the English passive; exact.
ʾăšer-ʾattâ morʾeh bāhār: a Hophal participle, rendered 'which you are being shown'. Closer to the Hebrew aspect than the ASV. taḇnîṯ 'pattern' is consistent with v 9.

None encodes the canon's 'residence built to the creators' plans' or its 'provisions for a resident team', which appear only in the labelled notes at 25:2, 9 and 22.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-proper-names: Option (a) for this wave: keep the split, do not retro-edit signed-off chapters, and record it in the corpus. For the later normalization pass the reviewer recommends one form per name across the corpus. Prefer the transliterated 'Moshe'/'Par'oh', because they are the only English forms left in an otherwise transliterated Torah and the ASV equivalence table already serves readers of the canon's KJV-based English. Prefer the tz spelling 'Mitzrayim', since tz is already the Torah rule for every other tsade. Keep 'the Egyptians' for the population (amend the central gentilic 'Mitsri', which no volume uses), and bring isaiah-woh 'Egypt' into the same decision.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-torah: Retire the transliterated 'torah' at the next Exodus pass and apply the sense rule. Ex 13:9 'the law of YHWH' is a Deuteronomic-style formula (ASV, NRSV 'law'), and Ex 16:4 'my law' (ASV, NRSV) or 'my instruction' (NJPS 'teaching') is a founder preference. Keep Isaiah's 'teaching' as the prophetic clause of the same central entry.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-bara: Agree. Keep 'create' outside Gen 1 (Deut 4:32; Isaiah 40-65 already do), and add a scope sentence to central bara saying that 'shape' is the Gen 1 rendering only.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-teruma: Ratify 'oblation' with hērîm 'set apart'. It is lexically sound, already the corpus term in Ezekiel and Isa 40:20, and it removes the unsupported 'heave' etymology. Semver: minor is defensible because no shipped line changes, but renumber the three parallel 2.84.0 diffs sequentially.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-merism: Confirm 'the heavens and the earth' for the merism outside Gen 1 (exodus-woh 20:11; Deut 4:26, 39). State explicitly that the creation formulas of Isaiah ('created the skies', 'spread out the earth') render the physical sky 'skies', so that the two practices read as one rule.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F6-saraf: The Isaiah wave has already applied the same rule ('a fiery flying serpent' at Isa 14:29; 'seraphim' for the Isa 6 attendants). Promote one central śārāp̄ entry stating both clauses.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F7-herem: The Former Prophets decision is now visible ('devoted thing' / 'devote to destruction'). Adopt it at Num 21:2-3 (reviewer revise), promote a single central ḥērem entry, and reconcile isaiah-woh 43:28 'the ban'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F8-deuteronomy-quotation: Confirm. It matches NJPS practice and the chapter applies it consistently (4:6, 10 inner double marks; 4:41 narration). Apply it unchanged to Deut 1-3 and 5.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F9-kapporet: Keep 'mercy-seat' (ASV, NRSV). It preserves the link with kippēr and Lev 16 that 'cover' loses, and the dispute is fully recorded in the commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F10-next-exodus-pass: Agree with all three items (16:16 'souls'; the 'heavens' register check at 16:4; 17:14; 20:4, 11, 19; 13:9 and 16:4 'torah'). Add the FP1 shofar refId correction (EXO-WOH-20:15, not 20:18) to the merge checklist.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

notes.official: The formula opens the long divine speech of Ex 25-31, the instructions for the sanctuary, which Ex 35-40 carries out almost word for word. 'Moses' follows `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`.

paragraphs.text: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיִקְחוּ־לִ֖י תְּרוּמָ֑ה מֵאֵ֤ת כָּל־אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדְּבֶ֣נּוּ לִבּ֔וֹ תִּקְח֖וּ אֶת־תְּרוּמָתִֽי׃

i18n.en: "Speak to the children of Yisra'el, that they take for me an oblation; from every man whose heart makes him willing you shall take my oblation.

notes.official:
*wəyiqḥû-lî tərûmâ* 'that they take for me an oblation' (draft and ASV 'an offering'). *tərûmâ*, from *rwm* in the Hiphil 'lift off, set apart', is a portion set apart from a person's goods for the sanctuary or the priests. The ASV's 'heave-offering' in Numbers reflects an explanation by a lifting gesture that the texts do not support (Milgrom, *Numbers*, JPS, 1990, excursus on the *tərûmâ*), and NJPS has 'gifts'. The central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus` renders *tərûmâ* 'oblation' in Ezekiel and reserved the Torah decision for this review; the wave extends 'oblation' to the Torah (Ex 25:2-3; Num 18), so that *tərûmâ* has one English word across the corpus and stays distinct from *qorbān* 'offering'. *ʾăšer yiḏḏəḇennû libbô* 'whose heart makes him willing': the contribution is voluntary (35:5, 21-29).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes vv 2-7 ('Of every man ... ye shall take an offering for me ... gold, and silver, and brass, (precious) stones, etc.') and reads the list as fresh food and riches requested by a team of creators residing on Earth. The line renders *tərûmâ* by the corpus term and the materials by their lexical senses; in the Hebrew the list is the material for the sanctuary that vv 8-9 go on to describe.

paragraphs.text: וְזֹאת֙ הַתְּרוּמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּקְח֖וּ מֵאִתָּ֑ם זָהָ֥ב וָכֶ֖סֶף וּנְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

i18n.en: And this is the oblation which you shall take from them: gold, and silver, and bronze;

notes.official: *zāhāḇ wāḵesep̄ ûnəḥōšeṯ* 'gold, and silver, and bronze' (draft and ASV 'brass'). *nəḥōšeṯ* is copper and its alloy with tin, bronze; brass, the copper-zinc alloy, was not worked in the Late Bronze and Iron Age Levant, and the ASV/KJV 'brass' is the older English name for bronze. The line uses 'bronze' (new central `nechoshet-bronze-copper-alloy-cross-corpus`), as 1-kings-woh 8:64 'the bronze altar' and NRSV do; NJPS has 'copper'. *tərûmâ* 'oblation' as v 2 (central qorbanot). The canon's English quotation of this verse follows the KJV 'brass' (French *cuivre*); see the reception note at v 2.

paragraphs.text: וּתְכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ וְעִזִּֽים׃

i18n.en: and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair;

notes.official: The dye terms keep the ASV (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`): *təḵēleṯ* 'blue' is a blue-violet dye from the murex snail, *ʾargāmān* 'purple' a red-purple murex dye, and *tôlaʿaṯ šānî* 'scarlet', literally 'worm of crimson', a dye from the kermes insect (Sarna 1991; Propp 2006); some versions have 'violet' for *təḵēleṯ*. *šēš* 'fine linen' is an Egyptian loanword (central `shesh-fine-linen-egyptian-loanword`). *ʿizzîm* is 'goats', and the material meant is their hair (26:7); the ASV brackets 'hair', and the line prints it without brackets. Reception: see the note at v 2.

paragraphs.text: וְעֹרֹ֨ת אֵילִ֧ם מְאָדָּמִ֛ים וְעֹרֹ֥ת תְּחָשִׁ֖ים וַעֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּֽים׃

i18n.en: and rams' skins dyed red, and sealskins, and acacia wood;

notes.official: *ʿōrōṯ ʾêlim məʾoddāmîm* 'rams' skins dyed red'. *ʿōrōṯ təḥāšîm* 'sealskins': *taḥaš* is unidentified. The proposals are Arabic *tuḫas* 'dugong, dolphin' (NJPS 'dolphin skins', and the ASV 'sealskins' belongs to the same line of explanation), Egyptian *ṯḥś* 'stretch (leather)' (NRSV 'fine leather'), and Akkadian *dušû*, a yellow-orange colour of leather or stone (Propp 2006); the KJV 'badgers' skins' follows the Talmud. The line keeps the ASV (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`). *ʿăṣê šiṭṭîm* 'acacia wood', the acacia of Sinai and the Aravah (KJV 'shittim wood'). Reception: see the note at v 2.

paragraphs.text: שֶׁ֖מֶן לַמָּאֹ֑ר בְּשָׂמִים֙ לְשֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֔ה וְלִקְטֹ֖רֶת הַסַּמִּֽים׃

i18n.en: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense;

notes.official: *šemen lammāʾōr* 'oil for the light', for the lampstand (27:20); *liqṭōreṯ hassammîm* 'for the sweet incense', literally 'the incense of spices' (30:34-38). The verse is lacking in the Septuagint of this passage (Wevers, *Notes on the Greek Text of Exodus*, 1990). Reception: see the note at v 2.

paragraphs.text: אַבְנֵי־שֹׁ֕הַם וְאַבְנֵ֖י מִלֻּאִ֑ים לָאֵפֹ֖ד וְלַחֹֽשֶׁן׃

i18n.en: onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod and for the breastplate.

notes.official: *ʾaḇnê-šōham* 'onyx stones': *šōham* is unidentified (onyx, carnelian and lapis lazuli have been proposed; cf. Gen 2:12, where it is a product of Chavilah). *ʾaḇnê millūʾîm* 'stones to be set', literally 'stones of filling', i.e. for mounting. *ʾēp̄ōḏ* 'ephod' and *ḥōšen* 'breastplate' (ASV; NRSV and NJPS 'breastpiece') are garments of the high priest (Ex 28). The ASV renderings are kept (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`). Reception: see the note at v 2.

paragraphs.text: וְעָ֥שׂוּ לִ֖י מִקְדָּ֑שׁ וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֖י בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

i18n.en: And let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst.

notes.official: *wəʿāśû lî miqdāš wəšāḵantî bəṯôḵām* 'And let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst'. *miqdāš* 'sanctuary, holy place', from *qdš*. *šāḵan* 'dwell' (central `shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`): the stated purpose of the sanctuary is presence among the people (cf. 29:45-46; 1 Kgs 6:13; 8:27), and the suffix is 'in their midst', not 'in it'.

paragraphs.text: כְּכֹ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ מַרְאֶ֣ה אוֹתְךָ֔ אֵ֚ת תַּבְנִ֣ית הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת תַּבְנִ֣ית כָּל־כֵּלָ֑יו וְכֵ֖ן תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings, so you shall make it.

notes.official:
*kəḵōl ʾăšer ʾănî marʾeh ʾôṯəḵā ʾēṯ taḇnîṯ hammiškān wəʾēṯ taḇnîṯ kol-kēlāyw* 'According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings'. *taḇnîṯ*, from *bnh* 'build', is a pattern, model or plan (new central `tabnit-pattern-model-cross-corpus`, which also governs v 40 and Deut 4:16-18; cf. 2 Kgs 16:10; 1 Chr 28:11-19). Whether Moses is shown a model, a plan or the heavenly sanctuary itself is debated. Gudea of Lagash, who receives the plan of the Eninnu temple in a dream (Cylinder A), is the closest ANE parallel for a divinely revealed design (Hurowitz, *I Have Built You an Exalted House*, 1992), and later readers took it as a heavenly original (Wis 9:8; Heb 8:5). *miškān*, literally 'dwelling', from the *šāḵan* of v 8, keeps the ASV term 'tabernacle' for the structure (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) summarizes the sanctuary instructions ('chapter XXVI of Exodus') as a residence the creators asked men to build 'according to their plans', in which they would meet the representatives of men. The line renders *taḇnîṯ* 'pattern' and *miškān* 'tabernacle' by their lexical senses and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֙צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And they shall make an ark of acacia wood: two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.

notes.official: *ʾărôn* 'ark' is a chest or box (the same word names Yosef's coffin, Gen 50:26), not the vessel of the Flood, which is *tēḇâ*. At about 45 cm to the cubit the chest measures some 1.1 x 0.7 x 0.7 m. The verb is plural ('they shall make'), while the following instructions address Moses in the singular; the LXX has the singular here.

paragraphs.text: וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עָלָ֛יו זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: And you shall overlay it with pure gold, inside and outside you shall overlay it; and you shall make upon it a crown of gold all around.

notes.official: *zēr zāhāḇ sāḇîḇ* 'a crown of gold all around': *zēr* is a moulding or rim (NJPS 'a gold molding'); the ASV 'crown' is kept.

paragraphs.text: וְיָצַ֣קְתָּ לּ֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וְנָ֣תַתָּ֔ה עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל־צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל־צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃

i18n.en: And you shall cast four rings of gold for it, and put them on its four feet: two rings on its one side, and two rings on its other side.

notes.official: *paʿămōṯāyw* 'its feet': *paʿam* is literally 'step, foot', here the lower corners of the chest (NJPS 'its four feet').

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בַדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב׃

i18n.en: And you shall make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

notes.official: *baddê ʿăṣê šiṭṭîm* 'poles of acacia wood' (ASV 'staves'): 'poles' is the rendering of the signed-off 1-kings-woh 8:7-8 for the same carrying poles of the ark (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

paragraphs.text: וְהֵֽבֵאתָ֤ אֶת־הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֥את אֶת־הָאָרֹ֖ן בָּהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And you shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark with them.

notes.official: The ark is carried by the poles and not touched (cf. Num 4:15; 2 Sam 6:6-7). 'Poles' as v 13 (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

paragraphs.text: בְּטַבְּעֹת֙ הָאָרֹ֔ן יִהְי֖וּ הַבַּדִּ֑ים לֹ֥א יָסֻ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: The poles shall be in the rings of the ark; they shall not be removed from it.

notes.official: *lōʾ yāsurû mimmennû* 'they shall not be removed from it': the ark's poles stay in the rings permanently, unlike those of the table and the altar (Num 4:6, 8); 1 Kgs 8:8 notes that their ends could be seen from the great hall.

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתָּ֖ אֶל־הָאָרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And you shall put into the ark the Testimony which I will give you.

notes.official: *hāʿēḏuṯ* 'the Testimony': the tablets of the covenant (31:18; 32:15), placed inside the ark, capitalised as exodus-woh 16:34 (`edut-the-testimony-capitalisation-torah`). NJPS 'the Pact' and NRSV 'the covenant' interpret the word through Akkadian *adê* 'treaty stipulations'.

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ כַפֹּ֖רֶת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר אַמָּתַ֤יִם וָחֵ֙צִי֙ אָרְכָּ֔הּ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי רָחְבָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And you shall make a mercy-seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth.

notes.official: *kappōreṯ zāhāḇ ṭāhôr* 'a mercy-seat of pure gold'. The word is formed from *kpr*, and its meaning is disputed: 'cover' (NJPS), the lid of the ark, or 'place of atonement', from *kippēr* 'make atonement', since the blood of the Day of Atonement is applied to it (Lev 16:14-15). The LXX *hilastērion* takes the second view, and Tyndale's 'mercy-seat', after Luther's *Gnadenstuhl*, follows that tradition (Milgrom 1991; Propp 2006). The line keeps the ASV, which NRSV also retains (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`). The *kappōreṯ* has the length and breadth of the ark (v 10) and is a separate piece of solid gold.

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֛יתָ שְׁנַ֥יִם כְּרֻבִ֖ים זָהָ֑ב מִקְשָׁה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם מִשְּׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃

i18n.en: And you shall make two cherubim of gold; of hammered work you shall make them, at the two ends of the mercy-seat.

notes.official: *šənayim kərūḇîm zāhāḇ miqšâ* 'two cherubim of gold; of hammered work' (ASV 'beaten work'). 'Cherubim' follows the central `cherubim-ezek`, whose rationale already names the ark cherubim of Ex 25:18-20; *miqšâ* is metal hammered from one piece (vv 31, 36; Num 8:4; 10:2; `tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`). The cherubim are the winged composite guardians of ANE iconography, winged sphinxes and lions flanking thrones (the Megiddo ivories; the Ahiram sarcophagus), not the putti of later art (Keel, *The Symbolism of the Biblical World*, 1978; Mettinger, *The Dethronement of Sabaoth*, 1982).

paragraphs.text: וַ֠עֲשֵׂה כְּר֨וּב אֶחָ֤ד מִקָּצָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וּכְרוּב־אֶחָ֥ד מִקָּצָ֖ה מִזֶּ֑ה מִן־הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֶת־הַכְּרֻבִ֖ים עַל־שְׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And make one cherub at the one end and one cherub at the other end; of one piece with the mercy-seat you shall make the cherubim on its two ends.

notes.official: *min-hakkappōreṯ taʿăśû ʾeṯ-hakkərūḇîm* 'of one piece with the mercy-seat you shall make the cherubim': literally 'from the mercy-seat', i.e. hammered out of the same piece rather than attached (Sarna 1991). Central `cherubim-ezek`.

paragraphs.text: וְהָי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֑יו אֶל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת יִהְי֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the cherubim shall spread out their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy-seat with their wings, with their faces each toward the other; toward the mercy-seat shall the faces of the cherubim be.

notes.official: *sōḵəḵîm bəḵanpêhem* 'overshadowing ... with their wings', from *skk* 'screen, cover'. The cherubim face each other and look down toward the *kappōreṯ*. In 1 Kgs 6:23-28 the Temple cherubim are separate and much larger figures standing in the inner sanctuary; here they are part of the ark's cover (central `cherubim-ezek`).

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתָּ֧ אֶת־הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת עַל־הָאָרֹ֖ן מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְאֶל־הָ֣אָרֹ֔ן תִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And you shall put the mercy-seat on top of the ark; and into the ark you shall put the Testimony which I will give you.

notes.official: The verse repeats v 16 and fixes the order: the Testimony inside the ark, the mercy-seat on top (*milmāʿlâ* 'above') (`edut-the-testimony-capitalisation-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וְנוֹעַדְתִּ֣י לְךָ֮ שָׁם֒ וְדִבַּרְתִּ֨י אִתְּךָ֜ מֵעַ֣ל הַכַּפֹּ֗רֶת מִבֵּין֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־אֲרֹ֣ן הָעֵדֻ֑ת אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֲצַוֶּ֛ה אוֹתְךָ֖ אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And there I will meet with you, and I will speak with you from above the mercy-seat, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the Testimony, all that I will command you for the children of Yisra'el.

notes.official:
*wənôʿaḏtî ləḵā šām* 'And there I will meet with you': *yʿd* (Niphal) 'meet by appointment' is the verb of *ʾōhel môʿēḏ* 'the tent of meeting' (29:42-43; 30:6, 36). *wəḏibbartî ʾittəḵā* 'and I will speak with you' (ASV 'commune with thee'). *mibbên šənê hakkərūḇîm* 'from between the two cherubim' is the place of the voice (Num 7:89) and, in the later title *yōšēḇ hakkərūḇîm* 'enthroned on the cherubim' (1 Sam 4:4; 2 Kgs 19:15), of the invisible throne (Mettinger 1982; central `cherubim-ezek`). 'The ark of the Testimony' (`edut-the-testimony-capitalisation-torah`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) describes the tent of meeting as the place where the creators met the representatives of men, who brought food and presents there. The line renders *nôʿaḏtî* 'I will meet' and *dibbartî* 'I will speak' by their lexical senses.

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ שֻׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And you shall make a table of acacia wood: two cubits its length, and a cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.

notes.official: *šulḥān* 'table', about 90 x 45 x 70 cm (two cubits by one by one and a half).

paragraphs.text: וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לּ֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: And you shall overlay it with pure gold, and make for it a crown of gold all around.

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ לּ֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ זֵר־זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: And you shall make for it a border of a handbreadth all around, and you shall make a crown of gold for its border all around.

notes.official: *misgeret ṭōp̄aḥ* 'a border of a handbreadth': a rim or frame about 7.5 cm wide (NJPS 'a rim').

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת־הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And you shall make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings on the four corners that are at its four feet.

paragraphs.text: לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן׃

i18n.en: Close by the border shall the rings be, as holders for the poles to carry the table.

notes.official: *ləḇāttîm ləḇaddîm* 'as holders for the poles', literally 'as houses for poles' (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֶת־הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְנִשָּׂא־בָ֖ם אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן׃

i18n.en: And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and the table shall be carried with them.

notes.official: 'Poles' as v 13 (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ קְּעָרֹתָ֜יו וְכַפֹּתָ֗יו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו֙ וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And you shall make its dishes, and its spoons, and its flagons, and its bowls, with which libations are poured; of pure gold you shall make them.

notes.official: *qəʿārōṯāyw wəḵappōṯāyw ûqəśôṯāyw ûmənaqqiyyōṯāyw* 'its dishes, and its spoons, and its flagons, and its bowls' (ASV); the identification of the four vessels is approximate (*kappôṯ* are small pans or ladles for incense, Num 7:14). *ʾăšer yussaḵ bāhēn* 'with which libations are poured' refers to the last two, the vessels for drink-offerings (cf. 37:16).

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתָּ֧ עַֽל־הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן לֶ֥חֶם פָּנִ֖ים לְפָנַ֥י תָּמִֽיד׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And you shall set upon the table the bread of the presence before me continually.

notes.official: *leḥem pānîm ləp̄ānay tāmîḏ* 'the bread of the presence before me continually' (draft and ASV 'showbread'). *leḥem pānîm* is literally 'bread of the face', and the verse plays on it with *ləp̄ānay* 'before my face'; the line uses 'the bread of the presence' (NRSV), so that the noun stays visible and links with the *pānîm* of 33:14-15 'my presence' (`panim-presence-face-convention-torah`; `tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`). 'Showbread' is Tyndale's coinage after Luther's *Schaubrot*; NJPS has 'bread of display'. The twelve loaves are described at Lev 24:5-9 (cf. 1 Sam 21:7 MT).

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מְנֹרַ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה תֵּעָשֶׂ֤ה הַמְּנוֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ׃

i18n.en: And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold; of hammered work shall the lampstand be made, its base and its shaft; its cups, its knobs, and its flowers shall be of one piece with it.

notes.official: *mənōraṯ zāhāḇ ṭāhôr* 'a lampstand of pure gold' (draft and ASV 'candlestick'). The *mənôrâ* carries oil lamps (v 37 *nērōṯêhā*), not candles, and 'lampstand' is the term of NRSV, NJPS and the commentaries (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`; C. L. Meyers, *The Tabernacle Menorah*, 1976). *yərēḵāh wəqānāh* 'its base and its shaft', literally 'its thigh and its reed'. *gəḇîʿêhā kap̄tōrêhā ûp̄əraḥêhā* 'its cups, its knobs, and its flowers' (ASV 'knops'). Meyers interprets the object as a stylized almond tree.

paragraphs.text: וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה ׀ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃

i18n.en: And six branches shall go out from its sides: three branches of the lampstand out of its one side, and three branches of the lampstand out of its other side;

notes.official: Six branches (*qānîm*, literally 'reeds') leave the central shaft, three on each side; 'lampstand' as v 31 (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

paragraphs.text: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בַּקָּנֶ֥ה הָאֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן־הַמְּנֹרָֽה׃

i18n.en: three cups made like almond-blossoms on the one branch, a knob and a flower; and three cups made like almond-blossoms on the other branch, a knob and a flower; so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

notes.official: *gəḇiʿîm məšuqqāḏîm* 'cups made like almond-blossoms': *məšuqqāḏ* is formed from *šāqēḏ* 'almond tree' (cf. the wordplay *šāqēḏ / šōqēḏ* of Jer 1:11-12, and Aharon's almond rod, Num 17:23 MT). 'Knob' modernizes the ASV 'knop' (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

paragraphs.text: וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And on the lampstand four cups made like almond-blossoms, its knobs and its flowers;

notes.official: *ûḇammənōrâ* 'and on the lampstand' itself, i.e. the central shaft, which carries four cups against three on each branch (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

paragraphs.text: וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּחַת־שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֙שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן־הַמְּנֹרָֽה׃

i18n.en: and a knob under two branches of one piece with it, and a knob under two branches of one piece with it, and a knob under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

notes.official: A knob sits beneath each pair of branches where they leave the shaft; the threefold repetition is the Hebrew's (`tabernacle-furnishings-vocabulary-exodus-25`).

paragraphs.text: כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה יִהְי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: Their knobs and their branches shall be of one piece with it; the whole of it one hammered work of pure gold.

notes.official: *kullāh miqšâ ʾaḥaṯ* 'the whole of it one hammered work': the lampstand is beaten from a single piece of gold (v 31).

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱלָה֙ אֶת־נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְהֵאִ֖יר עַל־עֵ֥בֶר פָּנֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And you shall make its lamps, seven; and they shall set up its lamps so that it gives light over against its front.

notes.official: *wəheʿĕlâ ʾeṯ-nērōṯêhā* 'and they shall set up its lamps': the Hebrew verb is singular and impersonal ('one shall raise'), rendered with the English impersonal 'they'. *heʿĕlâ* 'cause to go up' means either mounting the lamps on the branches or kindling them (27:20; 30:8; Lev 24:2), and the line keeps the neutral 'set up'. *wəhēʾîr ʿal-ʿēḇer pānêhā* 'so that it gives light over against its front', literally 'its face' (ASV 'over against it'): the lamps shine forward (Num 8:2-3).

paragraphs.text: וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: And its snuffers and its snuff-dishes shall be of pure gold.

notes.official: *malqāḥêhā ûmaḥtōṯêhā* 'its snuffers and its snuff-dishes' (ASV): tongs for trimming wicks and trays for the burnt ends (NJPS 'its tongs and fire pans').

paragraphs.text: כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made, with all these vessels.

notes.official: *kikkār* 'a talent', some 30-35 kg of gold. The verb *yaʿăśeh* 'he shall make' is impersonal, and the line uses the English passive.

paragraphs.text: וּרְאֵ֖ה וַעֲשֵׂ֑ה בְּתַ֨בְנִיתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה מָרְאֶ֖ה בָּהָֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And see, and make them after their pattern, which you are being shown on the mountain."

notes.official: *ûrəʾēh waʿăśēh bəṯaḇnîṯām ʾăšer-ʾattâ morʾeh bāhār* 'And see, and make them after their pattern, which you are being shown on the mountain'. *morʾeh* is a Hophal participle, present and continuous, 'being shown' (ASV 'which hath been showed thee'); the line follows the Hebrew aspect. *taḇnîṯ* 'pattern' as v 9 (central `tabnit-pattern-model-cross-corpus`). Heb 8:5 quotes the verse for the idea of an earthly copy of a heavenly sanctuary. The closing quotation mark ends the divine speech in this chapter file; the speech continues in Ex 26.
